findings.message: The harness reads committed fixtures from `eval/fixtures/`, which holds 18 fixture directories, and some of them are clean. Reaching 50 planted defects therefore needs either new committed fixtures under `eval/fixtures/` or a harness-local Author prompt plus runtime planting. The ticket names neither location. `eval/fixtures/` and any separate prompt file are outside the fence, so an implementer who follows the most natural route will escape scope.
findings.paved_road: State that the harness-local Author prompt is inline in `eval/harness.py` and that the defects are planted at runtime, so no fixture or prompt file is added. Otherwise, add the exact fixture or prompt paths to the Scope fence.

findings.message: Today `harness.run` appends a `review_baseline` NO-GO signal on every scored run. `test_run_scores_every_fixture_and_journals_the_no_go_signal` and `test_rerun_after_a_recorded_verdict_takes_a_fresh_sequence_and_calls_again` assert this, and `run_seq` is derived from the count of those signals. The ticket says only that operator-only `--record-go` appends the signal. It does not say whether ordinary runs keep journaling NO-GO. If they stop, a re-run would reuse the same effect keys and replay cached calls, which contradicts the rerun test. The ticket names neither of these tests for migration or preservation.
findings.paved_road: State explicitly that ordinary runs still append the NO-GO signal, `run_seq` keying is unchanged, and `--record-go` only appends an operator GO body. Otherwise, name the two tests to migrate and give the new `run_seq` source.

findings.message: The criterion 'preserve the required identity and reader boundary' cannot be checked as written. `resolve_baseline` binds only when the GO body has `tiers`, an `identity` keyed exactly `{review, author}` per tier matching `Registry(config)`, and integer `spec_major` for both surfaces equal to the majors of `specs/review.md` and `specs/author.md`. The harness's `ReviewBaselineSignal.verdict` is currently `Literal["NO-GO"]`. `tests/test_baseline.py` is not in Verification, so nothing guards the unfenced reader.
findings.paved_road: Rewrite the criterion to say that a `--record-go` body resolves to `GO`/`binds=true` through the unchanged `resolve_baseline`, that a non-operator path cannot write `verdict: GO`, and that the recorded `review_baseline` signal identity equals the report's verdict-signal identity. Add `tests/test_baseline.py` to Verification as a preservation suite.
